run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T14:54:14Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy was driven by a burst of error spans on frontend-proxy's server span 'ingress' between ~14:55Z and ~14:59Z (50-94 errors per 5m versus a pre-incident baseline of ~1-3 per 5m, ratio 0.0247 versus 0.000627 at 14:40Z). The errors are not generated inside frontend-proxy: its envoy logs show upstream responses, mostly 'POST /api/checkout' 500 via_upstream from the frontend upstream, while normal product/cart/recommendation requests returned 200. At 14:58Z the error spans line up with frontend 'POST /api/checkout' (90 per 5m), frontend client span 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' (90), checkout client span 'oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge' (47.8) and checkout server span 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' (47.8), while every other frontend operation had 0 error spans. The deepest supported cause is the payment Deployment: a rollout restart (pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T14:54:27Z, same image, replicas=1, no readiness/liveness/startup probe) created ReplicaSet payment-79d86bf97f and terminated the old pod payment-55766d76b9-5frt4 at 14:54:32Z; the replacement container logged 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080' only at 14:55:48Z and received its first Charge at 14:56:35Z, and payment span throughput dropped to 0 for the 14:57 and 14:58 minutes. With no readiness probe the new pod counted as Ready before it served, so checkout's Charge calls failed with no payment endpoint, frontend turned that into 500s on /api/checkout, and frontend-proxy recorded them as ingress error spans. A separate, pre-existing error mode also exists on frontend-proxy (envoy 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} on /api/data and /api/products) and was already present at 14:42:01Z, before the payment restart; it is background, not explained by this rollout, and its own root cause is unknown.

claims.text: frontend-proxy server span 'ingress' STATUS_CODE_ERROR increased from about 1-3 per 5m before 14:55Z to 50 (point 14:56:14Z), 91.11 (14:57:14Z), 94.44 (14:58:14Z) and 94.06 (14:59:14Z), then fell back to about 4.44 at 15:02:14Z; the client span 'router frontend egress' error series moved in parallel (0 before, 47.78 at 14:56:14Z, 88.89-90.7 at 14:57-14:59Z, 1.11 at 15:02:14Z).

At evaluation time 14:58:00Z (5m increases) frontend-proxy 'ingress' had 94.44 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans against 3722.22 STATUS_CODE_UNSET ingress spans, and 'router frontend egress' 90 error spans against 3726.67 unset; the resulting ingress error ratio is about 0.0247.

In the same 14:58:00Z 5-minute window the error spans line up along the checkout path: frontend 'POST /api/checkout' ERROR 90 versus 136.67 unset, frontend 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' ERROR 90, frontend 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' ERROR 90 versus 136.67 unset, checkout 'oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge' ERROR 47.78 versus 137.78 unset and checkout 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' ERROR 47.78 versus 137.78 unset; frontend's other operations (grpc CartService GetCart/AddItem, AdService GetAds, ProductCatalogService GetProduct, RecommendationService ListRecommendations, GET/POST /api/cart, GET /api/data, render route /) all report 0 error spans.

frontend-proxy envoy access logs show normal traffic being served by the 'frontend' upstream while checkout failed from it: 'POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 500 - via_upstream' at 14:56:27.417Z, 14:56:28.516Z and 14:56:29.333Z, alongside 'GET /api/cart 200', 'GET /api/products/... 200' and 'POST /api/cart 200' entries from the same upstream at the same seconds.

frontend-proxy also logged envoy-generated failures on other frontend routes: 'GET /api/products/OLJCESPC7Z HTTP/1.1" 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' at 14:55:24.832Z, 'GET /api/data/?contextKeys=binoculars ... 503 UC ...' at 14:57:18.297Z and 'GET /api/data/ ... 503 UC ...' at 14:57:18.421Z and 14:59:01.361Z.

The payment Deployment was rollout-restarted at 2026-11-16T14:54:27Z: Deployment otel-demo/payment is at generation 2 with observedGeneration 2, one replica and no readinessProbe/livenessProbe/startupProbe on container 'payment'; old ReplicaSet payment-55766d76b9 has 0 replicas and new ReplicaSet payment-79d86bf97f (1 replica, created 14:54:27Z) carries the pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T14:54:27Z, with the same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment and identical env/resources as the old ReplicaSet.

Payment rollout events: SuccessfulCreate 'Created pod: payment-79d86bf97f-9pm9t' 14:54:27Z and Scheduled 14:54:27Z, Created container 14:54:30Z, Started container 14:54:31Z; then Killing 'Stopping container payment' on payment-55766d76b9-5frt4 at 14:54:32Z, SuccessfulDelete of that pod 14:54:32Z and 'Scaled down replica set payment-55666d76b9' (payment-55766d76b9) from 1 to 0 at 14:54:32Z. No Evicted, OOMKilled, FailedScheduling, BackOff or Unhealthy events for payment appear in the window.

New payment pod payment-79d86bf97f-9pm9t logged 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080' at 14:55:48.791Z and its first 'Charge request received.' at 14:56:35.991Z (no payment log line before 14:55:48Z in the 14:54:00-14:57:00Z window), and it logged '14 UNAVAILABLE: Connection dropped' at 14:56:44.851Z; by 14:58:11-14:59:36Z it was continuously logging 'Charge request received.'/'Transaction complete.' pairs.

Payment span throughput collapsed during the restart: 1m increase of payment 'charge' / 'grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge' spans was 52-96 per minute from 14:45:00Z to 14:55:00Z, then 0 at 14:57:00Z and 0 at 14:58:00Z with no value returned at 14:59:00Z, and resumed at 72 at 15:00:00Z; payment's own error status counts ('GET', 'dns.lookup', 'tcp.connect', 'grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge' STATUS_CODE_ERROR) are 0 throughout, so calls did not reach a payment application that returned errors.

Baseline comparison for the same ratio (frontend-proxy 'ingress' STATUS_CODE_ERROR / all 'ingress' spans, 10m): 0.000627 at 14:40:00Z (window 14:30-14:40Z) and 0.002132 at 15:15:00Z (window 15:05-15:15Z), versus the about 0.0247 computed from the 14:58:00Z 5m values.

An error trace captured at 14:42:01Z, before the payment restart, shows the same frontend-proxy failure shape: load-generator 'GET' -> frontend-proxy 'ingress' with http.status_code=503 and error=true (494513 us) -> frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' with error="true" and http.status_code=0, i.e. no HTTP response from the frontend upstream.

Pods in otel-demo at query time: frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-b9w85 and frontend-675fd7b5c5-f44st are Running and ready with restartCount 0 and startTime 2026-11-16T14:22:31Z / 14:22:33Z; the payment Deployment's frontend-proxy and frontend counterparts are at Deployment generation 1 with image 2.1.3-frontend-proxy / 2.1.3-frontend, so neither frontend-proxy nor frontend was rolled out during the incident.

The observed frontend-proxy error-rate burst is caused by the payment Deployment rollout restart at 14:54:27Z: with a single replica and no readiness probe, the replacement pod was treated as Ready while its gRPC server was not yet listening (server start logged 14:55:48Z, first Charge 14:56:35Z) and payment span throughput was 0 in the 14:57Z/14:58Z minutes, so checkout's 'oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge' calls failed, checkout PlaceOrder and frontend 'POST /api/checkout' errored, and frontend-proxy recorded those frontend 500 responses as ingress error spans, lifting the ratio the alert evaluates from ~0.0006 to ~0.025.

A second, independent contributor keeps a small part of the frontend-proxy error rate: envoy returns 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} on frontend routes (/api/data, /api/products) when the frontend terminates the connection before responding. It was already present at 14:42:01Z before the payment restart and still appears at 14:59:01Z, so its root cause is not the payment rollout and is not determined by the available evidence.

Rejected: frontend-proxy itself failing or restarting. Its pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-b9w85 has restartCount 0, is Running/ready since 14:22:31Z, its Deployment is generation 1 with unchanged image 2.1.3-frontend-proxy, and its access log shows it successfully proxying 200 responses from the frontend upstream during the burst; the error spans mark responses/upstream attempts, not a fault in the proxy process.

Rejected: a general frontend application failure. At 14:58:00Z frontend's non-checkout operations report 0 error spans (grpc CartService GetCart 945.56 and AddItem 620 unset, AdService GetAds 298.89, ProductCatalogService GetProduct 3052.22, RecommendationService ListRecommendations 292.22, GET /api/cart 325.56, GET /api/data 298.89, render route / 102.22, all with STATUS_CODE_ERROR 0), so frontend errors are confined to the checkout path that depends on payment.

Rejected: the payment pod crashed, was OOMKilled or evicted. Its replacement pod has restartCount 0 and is Running/ready, its log shows a normal startup ('payment gRPC server started on port 8080') with no error or panic lines, and the only payment pod termination recorded is the controller's own 'Killing'/'Deleted pod'/'Scaled down replica set payment-55766d76b9 from 1 to 0' sequence at 14:54:32Z.

frontend-proxy error spans were not zero before the payment restart: the 'ingress' error series already carried 1.11-3.33 per 5m from about 13:55Z to 14:55Z and the 10m error ratio at 14:40:00Z was 0.000627, so a pre-existing non-zero error source exists and the alert's firing instant cannot be attributed to the payment rollout alone.

gaps: The alert rule 'RequestErrorRate' was not found in Prometheus rules (list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned status no_data), so the exact expression, labels, threshold and lookback behind the reported value 0.01111111111111111 are unknown; the reported start 2026-11-16T14:54:14Z is also 13 s earlier than the rollout restart annotation restartedAt=2026-11-16T14:54:27Z.

Jaeger returned no traces for the burst window: traces_search_by_tags for frontend-proxy operation 'ingress' with error=true/http.status_code=503 in 14:54:00-15:03:00Z and for checkout with error=true in the same window both returned no data, so there is no per-request 500-vs-503 breakdown of the burst; the only error trace available was at 14:42:01Z.
The frontend pod's log query for error keywords in 14:50-15:12Z returned no lines with tool status no_data (not citable), so frontend-side application error text during the burst is unverified.

kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready / kube_deployment_status_replicas_available were not evaluated as time series, so the exact count of Ready payment replicas between 14:54:32Z and 14:56:35Z is inferred from events, logs and span gaps rather than measured.

The reason the replacement payment container needed from 14:55:48Z (gRPC server announced) to 14:56:35Z (first Charge) is not determined; the only related log line is '14 UNAVAILABLE: Connection dropped' at 14:56:44Z, and the pre-restart container's logs are unavailable (no previous container instance was returned).

The root cause of the recurring frontend connection resets (503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}) is not determined; no frontend-side evidence explains why the frontend terminated those connections.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so whether the 14:54:27Z rollout restart and the earlier 14:22Z namespace-wide pod creation were planned changes cannot be verified.
next_steps: Add a readinessProbe (and a startupProbe) for the payment container and for the other otel-demo services that lack one, so a replacement pod is not marked Ready before its gRPC port accepts connections.
Run payment with more than one replica and set an explicit rollingUpdate maxUnavailable so a rollout restart cannot leave zero serving endpoints.
Review why payment's gRPC listener and first served request lagged container start by about 65-125 s, including its flagd connection setup and the '14 UNAVAILABLE: Connection dropped' line.
Investigate the recurring envoy 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} on /api/data and /api/products separately from the payment incident.
Confirm the RequestErrorRate alert expression, threshold and lookback in Alertmanager/Prometheus, since it reports 'above 0' and fires on a small background error level.
